notices.html: Terhune Orchards' Fall Family Fun Weekends need timed tickets: book online for $19.95 per person to beat the $24.95 door price. Runs Saturdays and Sundays through November 1.

Von Thun Farms' Fall Festival price is up now that opening weekend is over: $21.99 per person online ($24.99 at the door) in September, and the one free grandparent per paid admission deal ended after last weekend.

Liberty Science Center's planetarium reopens this Saturday, September 26: new laser projectors after weeks of upgrades, still the biggest planetarium in the hemisphere. Book timed tickets online first.

blurbs.terhune: This weekend: Fall Family Fun Weekends continues Saturdays and Sundays through November 1, 10am to 5pm, with wagon rides 10am to noon, a hay bale maze, corn maze, pumpkin patch and flower trails. Apple and peach picking are out for the season again this year after the spring freeze, so it's pumpkins and flowers instead. Tickets run $19.95 per person in advance online or $24.95 at the door, kids under 3 free. Call 609-924-2310 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.leeturkey: This weekend: apples are still ready to pick, Cortland, Empire, Fuji, Gala, Golden Delicious, Jonagold, Red Delicious and Stayman, plus tomatoes are still coming in. This is a simple, no-frills PYO farm with no festival extras, and the fields close for entry at 5:15pm. Call 609-448-0629 to confirm before you head over.
blurbs.vonthun: This weekend: the Fall Festival is in full swing with the Dogs and Dinos corn maze, hayrides, pedal karts, duck races and a pumpkin patch, Saturdays and Sundays 10am to 5pm through November 8, last ticket sold at 4pm. Now that opening weekend is over, admission is $21.99 per person online or $24.99 at the door, kids free until age 3, and the free-grandparent promo has ended. Call 732-329-8656 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.emerys: This weekend: the 2-acre Treasure Hunt corn maze, a straw-bale maze and the pumpkin display open for the season on Saturday, running daily 10am to 5pm through October 30, with hayrides on weekends. U-pick blueberry season is long over, but fresh and frozen berries are still sold in the farm market. Call 609-758-8514 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.battleview: This weekend: still no pick-your-own tree fruit after the spring freeze wiped out apples, cherries, peaches and nectarines, but pumpkin picking and weekend hayrides have started, along with a sunflower field for cutting your own. Call 732-462-0756 to confirm current hours and crop before you go.
blurbs.johnsons: This weekend: the Fall Harvest Festival continues through October 31 (plus Columbus Day) with apple and pumpkin picking, a family corn maze, gem mining, duck races and live music from noon to 4pm on weekends. Hayride tickets run $10 online or $12 at the door on weekends. Call the Pick Your Own Hotline 609-654-5894 to confirm before you go.
blurbs.dinosafari: This weekend: still closed for the season, since it only ran July 1 through August 16. It's expected to return next summer, so there's no need for a special trip until then.
blurbs.gfs: This weekend: a new indoor mural exhibit by artist Shantell Martin just opened on September 20 alongside the usual roaming peacocks and sculpture grounds, added reason for a visit if you haven't been in a while.
blurbs.lsc: This weekend: the Jennifer Chalsty Planetarium reopens Saturday, September 26, with new laser projectors after being closed for upgrades, still the biggest planetarium in the hemisphere. Book timed tickets online first.

events.title: Hopewell Tour Des Arts
events.desc: Stroll a small town full of open art studios and live bands at four stages, with the Sourland Mountains as a backdrop, a relaxed way to spend an afternoon outdoors.

events.title: Princeton Porchfest
events.desc: Wander from porch to porch listening to local musicians all over town, an easy free afternoon that doesn't need advance planning.

events.title: Mercer County Library Book Festival
events.desc: Meet local authors and browse tables full of books at the library's second annual festival, a low-key morning that's easy on the budget.

events.title: Etsch Farms Flashlight Night
events.note: $15.99 plus fee, ages 3 and up, check site for ticket availability
events.desc: Run the 8-acre corn maze after dark with flashlights, a fun twist on a fall farm outing for kids who think they've outgrown daytime mazes.
